date_note: Newsway (23 November) says the Financial Services Commission decided the fine at its regular meeting that day ('이날').
exec: Korea's financial regulator fined Lotte Card for under-disclosing a hacking-related data leak risk to bond investors, a reminder that breach risk belongs in securities filings.
geo_basis: regulator seat; the source names the Financial Services Commission, not a city
plain: South Korea's financial regulator fined Lotte Card "약 10억 2000만원", according to Newsway, for not properly warning bond investors that its 2025 hack could have leaked customer data.
summary: According to Newsway, citing financial authorities, South Korea's Financial Services Commission decided on 23 November to fine Lotte Card "약 10억 2000만원" for breaching Capital Markets Act disclosure duties. Regulators judged it could have recognised the possible leak from its 2025 hack when issuing bonds in September 2025, but did not adequately warn investors. The hack leaked data of "약 297만명" customers, Newsway says. A Lotte Card official said leakage was unconfirmed at filing time.
title: Korean regulator fines Lotte Card for under-disclosing hacking risk in bond filing

validation.note: One publisher read (Newsway, citing financial authorities and quoting a Lotte Card official). The Financial Services Commission's own release was not found or read; searches found no second report of the decision.

key_findings: Financial Services Commission fined Lotte Card "약 10억 2000만원" for Capital Markets Act disclosure violations, per Newsway.
Regulators found the possible data leak from the 2025 hack was not adequately disclosed to investors when it issued bonds in September 2025.

evidence.quote: 23일 금융당국에 따르면 금융위원회는 이날 정례회의를 열고 롯데카드의 자본시장법상 공시의무 위반에 대해 약 10억 2000만원의 과징금 부과를 의결했다.
해당 해킹 사고로 개인정보가 유출된 고객은 약 297만명에 달한다.
이어 17일 총 1700억원 규모의 회사채를 발행했다고 공시했다.
